newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. purchase lifts Lend Lease gearing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. purchase lifts Lend Lease gearing.

text.p: Property and insurance group Lend Lease Corp Ltd said on Thursday its US$400 million acquisition of Equitable Cos Inc's real estate unit would lift gearing, but was self-financing.

Lend Lease said the purchase of Equitable Real Estate Investement Management (ERE) would be funded through debt, including an eight-year US$100 million note to the Equitable, and existing cash reserves.
Finance director Robert Tsenin said the deal would take gearing to about 17 percent on December 1996 figures.

"It's important to note, though...that it is self financing, which means the free cash flow is larger than the interest payments, so the interest cover ratios will remain very strong," Tsenin told a media briefing.
ERE is the largest real estate manager in the U.S., managing about US$25 billion in property and mortgages for U.S. and international investors, including private and public pension funds.
Under the agreement, Lend Lease will continue to manage the Equitable's General Account real estate and mortgage porfolio, which has a current value of about A$10 billion.
Lend Lease chief executive David Higgins said that because of this the aquisition was a partnership, rather than a simple sale.
He declined to specify the details of the contract with Equitable but said it provided long security of tenure. "This is an agreement that gives us sufficient comfort," Higgins said.
Lend Lease said it expected the transaction to be completed by the end of June 1997.
Lend Lease shares ended 22 cents higher at A$22.75.
